heading: The standard menus
body:
The macOS host builds the menu bar itself, so every app has the menus that a Mac user expects. The app menu has About, Hide (Command-H), Hide Others (Option-Command-H), Show All and Quit (Command-Q). Quit is the normal macOS quit, so the app cleans up once. The File menu has Close Window (Command-W). The Edit menu has Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All; they act on the field that has the focus. The View menu has Enter Full Screen, the Window menu has Minimize (Command-M), Zoom and Bring All to Front, and the Help menu has the system search.

The host adds no New, Open, Save or Print item, because a Tachyon app has no document type. Your own items cannot take a shortcut of these standard commands.

On Linux and Windows the host shows a menu bar only when the manifest declares at least one item, so an app without menus keeps its plain window. That menu bar has File (your File items, then Close Window, Ctrl+W, and Quit, Ctrl+Q; Windows calls it Exit), and View and Help when they have items. There is no Edit menu: the web view handles Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All itself. iOS and Android have no menu bar, so they refuse declared menu items at build time (`TY1601`).

Linux menus and application services are tested by building and running the real GTK 4 and WebKitGTK 6.0 host. The Windows host is generated and compile-checked, but it has not been run on Windows yet, and Windows on ARM64 is not a tested target.
